context: Decision: a metadata store over the storage interface reads and writes instance records, snapshot records, and generation metadata in the primary storage of the instance. Every write after the first is a compare and swap on the version read; the first write is a create-if-absent. The storage interface returns no version with the bytes, so a read takes one Stat before the bytes, and a write takes one Stat after its flush under the live lease. Today only a test local store offers compare and swap; S3 and GCS stores come later. The title: Instance metadata sits beside the user data on a compare-and-swap store, and reads from the bucket alone.
